To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a principled robust and accurate sparse deep neural network (DNN) by combining the relaxed augmented Lagrangean based algorithms for DNN compression and the Feynman–Kac (FK) formalism for robust and sparse DNs.

we can at least improve the accuracy of adversarially robust ResNet20 for the CIFAR10 dataset by 5.4\% under 20 iterations of the IFGSM attack, and we can at least increase the channel sparsity by 2x for the same robust ResNet20, while improving its natural accuracy by 7.6\% as well.

we can develop a co-design for efficient DNN compression and principled sparse neural architectures for both robust and accurate deep neural nets, by leveraging the relaxed augmented Lagragian based algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of principled sparse and robust DNNs for robust deep learning.
a co-design of principled robustness and efficient compression, which can be potentially applied to other DNN compression algorithms.
the co-design of efficient algorithms for the Feynmann-Kac formalism based robust DNN compression, which is a promising avenue to achieve the robustness and efficiency in deep neural nets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed algorithms can achieve a better tradeoff between robustness and efficiency, compared with other state-of-the-art algorithms.

the proposed co-design of efficient and principled robust and accurate deep neural nets (DANs) compression algorithm can significantly improve the channel sparsity, while maintaining the robustness and accuracy of adversarially-trained DNNs.

our proposed channel pruning for the Feynmann-Kac formalism robustly trained DNs, can significantly improve both natural and robust accuracy, while maintaining a high sparsity level of the DNNs, thus, achieving a co-design of robustness, accuracy and efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Feynman- Kac formalism based robust and sparse DNs can be efficiently compressed with a relaxed augmented Lagrangians based channel pruning.
we can achieve both robustness and efficiency in the training of DNNs.
we can achieve the state-of-the-art robust accuracy on ResNet20 for the benchmark CIFAR10 adversarial attacks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sparsity meets robustness, and that we can achieve both sparsity and adversarial robustness in deep learning.
the co-design of sparsity and robust DNNs can lead to more robust and accurate deep neural architectures.
sparsity and robust training can be co-designed to achieve both efficiency and accuracy, which may open up new opportunities in the design and training of robust DNNs.
